clue.text: A painter's underwear

definitions.meaning: Stanley ... was an English painter of the twentieth century
a close-fitting woollen vest worn under clothing

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two definitions; Stanley Spencer painted Cookham village scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the surname of the artist Stanley Spencer, and an old-fashioned name for a warm undervest.

clue.text: Ella and Sid changed and dashed out

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two names are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Two friends, Ella and Sid, swapped clothes and rushed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The names look like the people doing the dashing, but they are only letters to rearrange; 'and' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To sally is to rush out suddenly, as troops do from a besieged fort.

clue.text: A fall in the main

parts.note: the main is old poetic language for the sea, and a fall there is the outgoing drop of the water level

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly'; here the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding tide is a lowering of the sea, which 'the main' names poetically.

clue.text: A dog's to be seen about-or a regular soldier

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: Someone notices a dog wandering around, or perhaps a soldier on patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', and 'to be seen' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small Welsh herding breed, famous as a royal pet.

clue.text: Orientals breaking family ties

indicators.note: breaking suggests the word Orientals is smashed and its pieces reassembled

explanation.surface: People from the East are cutting their bonds with their kin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks like a verb acting on 'family ties' but rearranges ORIENTALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives, the people one is connected to by blood or marriage, are family ties.

clue.text: A priest turning to tramp

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of A PRIEST are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes up the life of a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning to' reads as 'becoming', but 'turning' rearranges A PRIEST and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily, a verb sense of trudge.

clue.text: Material for over-sentimental dunderhead

parts.note: twee means cloyingly sweet or sentimental
the head, or first letter, of the word dunder

explanation.surface: A dull fool chooses a soppy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' splits into 'dunder' and 'head': its head is D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Detain suspect

definitions.meaning: to arrest or take into custody
to fear or anticipate, as in sensing trouble ahead

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'suspect' as a noun to be held; in the second sense it is a verb, to sense or fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to arrest a person, and to dread or perceive something likely.

clue.text: Veronese gentleman-a changeable character

definitions.meaning: one of Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona
in Greek myth the sea god who could change his shape at will

explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronese' might suggest the painter Paolo Veronese, but here it means from Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a Shakespearean character from Verona and to the shape-shifting Greek sea deity.

clue.text: A builder giving direction to a clerk

parts.note: E stands for east, a compass direction
clerk is an old word for a clergyman, here a parish rector

explanation.surface: A construction worker gives instructions to an office clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clerk' looks like an office worker; in its old sense, a 'clerk in holy orders', it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is one who puts up structures, so a builder.

clue.text: Kind that appears progressive

definitions.meaning: favouring reform and individual freedom in politics

explanation.walkthrough: 'that appears' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: generous in giving, and politically open to reform and change.

clue.text: Go off to labour in the river

indicators.note: in places the word for labour inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
to plod is to work slowly and steadily

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to toil away down by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links; the Exe flows through Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst violently, as a bomb does, is to go off.

clue.text: Introduced into it, one took in hundreds

parts.note: into gives the simple preposition in
I is the Roman numeral one
to take in food is to eat it, past tense ate
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, used loosely for hundreds

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being brought into a group after a hundred-strong feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced into it' reads as one phrase, but only 'Introduced' defines; 'it' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate someone is to admit them formally into a society.

clue.text: The student's leave of absence from lunch maybe

parts.note: ex means from, as in ex works
to lunch is one example of eating

explanation.surface: A student gets time off from college for a midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeat is Latin for 'let him go out', used at British schools and colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is formal permission for a pupil to be away from school or college.

clue.text: Note the evidence of a hard blow remained

parts.note: D is a musical note

parts.words: the evidence of a hard blow
parts.note: a welt is a raised mark on the skin left by a blow

explanation.surface: A record of a heavy punch still lingered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like 'observe' but is the musical note D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to stay or live in a place, so dwelt means stayed.

clue.text: A health-worker may find a trip's the answer

indicators.note: the answer is the solution these letters work out to once rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as a plain S, giving the letters of trips

explanation.surface: A counsellor might suggest a holiday as the cure.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange A TRIP'S THE, keeping the S; 'may find' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients, so is a kind of health professional.

clue.text: The autocrat finding love prospers-that's as it should be

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: the phrase hints that the letters of prospers are put right, arranged into their proper order

explanation.surface: A dictator thrives on love, and quite rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' only links; O (love) with PROSPERS rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant who rules harshly is one who keeps people down.

clue.text: By one take the measure of all around

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral one
to meter something is to measure it

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up the surroundings one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter is the boundary that runs right round a shape or area.

clue.text: He's put right concerning a theatre worker

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a dresser helps actors with costumes backstage

explanation.surface: Someone has been corrected about a backstage helper.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: one who puts things right, read as 'he who's put right'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rights wrongs or remedies grievances is a redresser.

clue.text: Splendid way of getting rent

definitions.meaning: rent here is torn, the past participle of rend

explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; here it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: dated slang for marvellous, and tearing, the action by which cloth is rent.

clue.text: Loot might be piled so

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters given could form another word if reordered

explanation.surface: Stolen goods could be heaped up this way.
explanation.walkthrough: PILED SO rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder or rob, the verb sense of loot.

clue.text: The waste is very large among doctors

indicators.note: among puts the size abbreviation inside the doctors

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, plural Drs
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Doctors are surrounded by enormous amounts of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very large' is a clothing-label size, not a quantity of waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless matter, the scum skimmed from molten metal.

clue.text: A coat that will last longer?

definitions.meaning: a garment worn over all the others
to outlast something by lasting through more use

explanation.walkthrough: 'that' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an overgarment worn over other clothing, and a verb for enduring beyond another.

clue.text: Not lit up naturally!

parts.note: natural light comes from the sky's star, so a place with no daylight is meant

explanation.walkthrough: 'lit up' could suggest drunk; here it is plain illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A place without daylight receives no natural illumination.

clue.text: Old Turkish governor planting a tree in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: planting puts the tree into the state's abbreviation, like setting it in soil

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: An Ottoman official puts in a sapling in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links; the planting image is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official or provincial governor.

clue.text: The fool will go easy on the heavyweight

indicators.note: on places the weight after the word for easy, as in a down clue

parts.note: simple means easy
a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: An idiot goes gently on a large opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go easy on' reads as one idiom, but 'easy' and 'on' do separate jobs; 'will go' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish or gullible person.

clue.text: A novelist's long tale with a point

parts.note: a saga is a lengthy story
N is north, a compass point

explanation.surface: A writer's long story has a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Françoise Sagan wrote Bonjour Tristesse; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Françoise Sagan was a French author of fiction.

clue.text: The French six-footer didn't stand erect

parts.note: le is French for the
an ant is an insect with six legs

explanation.surface: A tall Frenchman slouched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall man; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean is to tilt rather than stand straight up.

clue.text: Pressing for a smart appearance

parts.note: pressing here is smoothing creases out of clothes with a hot iron, not urging

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' could mean urgent; here it is household laundry work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing presses garments flat so the wearer looks neat.

clue.text: A high-flier may depend on it

definitions.text: A high-flier may depend on it

parts.words: A high-flier may depend on it
parts.note: a high-flier here is a circus acrobat swinging on a bar high above the ring, not an ambitious person

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' usually means a successful person; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus acrobat literally hangs from this swinging bar.

clue.text: This could well help one to get set

definitions.text: This could well help one to get set

parts.words: This could well help one to get set
parts.note: a substance used in cooking to make jellies firm

explanation.walkthrough: 'get set' sounds like a race start; here it is a jelly setting.
explanation.definitionFit: This protein makes liquids set into a jelly.

clue.text: The heartless rogue goes for interest

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of rogue, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: goes as a noun are turns, as in having goes at a game

explanation.surface: A cruel scoundrel makes a play for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' and 'for' only link; 'goes' is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns are the profit or yield on an investment, like interest.
